deep.reconstruction:
Context. The page has two layers. (a) In ink, a French draft of a rental note: 'Monsieur, Je prends votre appartement sur le premier étage pour quatre mois à raison de treize francesconi per mensem, du 20me de Mai jusqu'au 20me de septembre 1864 sous les conditions convenues.' This fits Riemann's stay in Pisa in 1863–65; the previous folio carries the address 'Pisa. Via della Maddalena 25'. It dates the sheet to around spring 1864. (b) In faint pencil, notes on the vanishing of the Riemann theta function. These are preparatory to 'Ueber das Verschwinden der Theta-Functionen' (Crelle 65, 1865/66).

Notation (Riemann's, as in his 1857 Abelian functions paper). u_1,...,u_p are normalized integrals of the first kind on a surface T' cut along a_nu, b_nu. Their periods are pi*i*delta_{nu,mu} along a_mu and a_{nu,mu} along b_mu. The theta function is theta(v_1..v_p) = sum over integer m of exp(sum a_{mu,mu'} m_mu m_mu' + 2 sum m_nu v_nu). A superscript mu on u or alpha (u_1^mu, alpha_1^mu) means the value of u_1 at the mu-th point eta_mu, or at the fixed point eps_mu respectively.

Line 1: theta(sum_{mu=1}^m u_1^mu - sum_{mu=1}^m alpha_1^mu + v_1, ...). This is a theta function whose argument is v shifted by the Abel–Jacobi image of the divisor eta_1+...+eta_m - eps_1-...-eps_m, viewed as a function of the m moving points.

Line 2 (crossed out): theta(v).

Line 3: theta(alpha_1 - u_1 + v_1, ..., alpha_p - u_p + v_p). This is the special case m = 1, i.e. theta(u(eps) - u(z) + v) as a function of the two points eps (giving alpha) and z (giving u). The superscripts here are hard to read.

Lines 4–5, a statement in German, roughly: 'If theta(v_1,...,v_p) = 0 and theta(alpha_1 - u_1 + v_1, ...) does not vanish identically for every value of (eps, epsilon) and (z, zeta) ...' (the end is illegible). This is the case distinction at the heart of the vanishing paper (my completion). Suppose theta(v) = 0. Then F(z) = theta(u(eps) - u(z) + v) vanishes at z = eps, because F(eps) = theta(v) = 0. If F is not identically zero, then by Riemann's 1857 count it has exactly p zeros on T'. So eps is one of them, and the others give v congruent to sum_{i=1}^{p-1} alpha^{(i)} - K, modulo periods (K = Riemann constant, up to sign convention). This yields Riemann's theorem: theta(v) = 0 exactly when v lies in W_{p-1} translated by the Riemann constant. In the degenerate case theta(u(eps) - u(z) + v) vanishes identically. One then passes to the m-point expression of line 1 and takes the smallest m for which it is not identically zero. That gives the general statement: theta(sum_{1}^{m} (alpha^mu - u^mu) + v) is identically zero for m below a threshold, which governs the order of vanishing.

No computation is actually carried out on this page. The next folio computes the Riemann constant, K_nu = sum_mu (1/(pi i)) ∫_{a_mu} u_nu^- du_mu + (a_{nu,nu} + pi i)/2, by integrating u_nu d log theta around the boundary of T'. That is the companion step.
errors: No mathematical errors can be assessed; the page contains only expressions and a condition statement, not derivations.
In line 3 a superscript was written and then overwritten (alpha_1^{mu} corrected). The pencil is faint and the final words of the German condition are uncertain.

results.what: Theta with argument v + sum_{mu=1}^m (u(eta_mu) - u(eps_mu)), studied as a function of the points, under the hypothesis theta(v)=0 and the case split on whether theta(u(eps)-u(z)+v) vanishes identically
results.modern_name: Riemann vanishing theorem (Theta divisor = W_{g-1} + kappa; multiplicity via identically-vanishing translates)

results.what: Dating evidence: Pisa rental draft, May–Sept 1864, on the same sheet as theta-vanishing notes

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics consists of preparatory notes for Riemann's own published 1865 vanishing-theorem paper. The only modest interest is the dating to Pisa, spring 1864, given by the rental note.

checkable.asserts: In genus 1 with Riemann's normalization, theta(v)=sum exp(a n^2+2 n v) vanishes at v=(a+pi i)/2. This is the half-period value matching the constant term (a_{nu,nu}+pi i)/2 of K_nu on the next folio; the result should be about 0.
Quasi-periodicity theta(v+a)=exp(-a-2v) theta(v), which underlies the zero count; the result should be about 0.
Periodicity theta(v+pi i)=theta(v); the result should be about 0.

transcription_corrections: Line 1 reads theta(Σ_1^m u_1^μ − Σ_1^m α_1^μ + v_1 ...); the upper summation limit is m (the second may be read as m or n). The closing bracket is missing in the manuscript.
The crossed-out line is likely 'ϑ(v)' or 'ϑv'.
In line 3 the superscripts on α_1 and u_1 are uncertain (possibly 1 or μ rather than p). The formula is most naturally theta(α_1 − u_1 + v_1, ...).

In the German statement the second theta argument is 'ϑ(α_1 − u_1 + v_1, ....)', with an overwritten superscript on α. 'nicht identisch' is correct. The second line reads 'für jeden Werth von ε, z und ε, ζ ...' (the points ε, z with their projections). The final words are illegible; possibly 'gleichzeitig' (struck) followed by a verb such as 'verschwindet'.
The ink heading 'Monsieur' and 'sous les conditions convenues' are correct. The currency is 'francesconi' (the Tuscan francescone).
